title: Zones of overlap between representative species are narrow

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Zones of overlap between representative species are narrow

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Where closely allied or representative species replace each other over a continuous area, the neutral territory between them is generally narrow compared with the territory occupied by each, and species become somewhat abruptly rarer towards their range limits.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: On the Origin of Species by Means of Natural Selection, or the Preservation of Favoured Races in the Struggle for Life

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: Hence the neutral territory between two representative species is generally narrow in comparison with the territory proper to each.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci Origin of Species claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Charles Darwin, On the Origin of Species (1st ed., London: John Murray, 1859), Chapter VI, “Difficulties on Theory”; section “Absence or rarity of transitional varieties.”. Scope: representative species on continents, mountains and sea depths

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on darwin1859-ch06-02: resolvable-now, resolvability 0.78

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The geometric and abundance predictions are direct and large public datasets provide broad coverage. Standard occupancy models can account for effort, allowing a decisive present-day test across many species pairs.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Estimate range widths and overlap-zone widths for geographically replacing close relatives, and fit abundance changes toward each boundary. Overlap zones consistently narrow relative to each range and abrupt edge declines support the claim; broad overlap or gradual transitions refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Occurrence density reflects observer effort as well as abundance.

Hybrid zones and patchy habitat complicate a single overlap-width measure.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
operationalizability: 0.86
discriminating power: 0.73
data adequacy: 0.68
analysis feasibility: 0.78
data existence: 0.84

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Contact-zone width and edge steepness are direct geographic measurements, and bird data are already sufficient for a large comparative test. The stated scope also includes mountains and sea depths, where occurrence density and abundance are much weaker, so the full scope is not covered. Sampling and species concepts are real biases, but they do not make the bird-scale result uninformative.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: For sister or representative species, measure the width of the zone where both occur relative to each species' range, and the steepness of abundance decline at the edge. Narrow contact zones and abrupt abundance drops would confirm the claim; overlap widths that are a large fraction of range width, or gradual declines, would refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Abundance, needed for abrupt rarity, is dense for birds and coarse for most other groups.

Depth zonation and deep-sea sister species are sparsely sampled.

Taxonomic splitting can manufacture narrow contacts between newly named species.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:

data adequacy: 0.58
discriminating power: 0.6
data existence: 0.8
